You use phrasal verbs to give a new meaning to a verb by adding a preposition or an adverb.

Phrasal verbs do not follow any specific rule; you just have to memorize them and learn their meanings. They are composed by a verb and a preposition or adverb.

There are some phrasal verbs that are separable, this means that you can separate the verb from the preposition or adverb when the action affects directly an object or object pronoun ( me, you, him, her, it, us, them.)

Example:

Turn off

The system is programmed to turn off the updates.
The system is programmed to turn the updated off .

The system is programmed to turn it off . (Correct)
The system is programmed to turn off it. (Incorrect)

Some other phrasal verbs inseparable, so these words need to remain together, they cannot be separated.

Example:
Work on

We are working on a new architecture style.

Event-Based, Layered Systems, Repository Architecture Styles
Among the architecture styles, we find event-based, layered and repository . They were all designed with a collection of procedures and functions for their components to interact with each other.

Event-based Style

This system is based on actors, constraint satisfaction, daemons, and packet-switched networks. Whenever it is necessary, components announce events instead of invoking direct procedures due to the fact that each event brings implicitly all the essential procedures for the component. A debugger, which is a program designed to clear errors, is an example of this style. Instead of announcing the procedures to take, it shows an event. Event-based programs provide a strong support for the system's evolution.

Layered Style

This style is organized hierarchically; the software functionality is divided into layers and these layers provide services to the one above and receive services from the one below. This style sees the system as a whole and is able to provide detailed information about each layer and its connections. An example of this style is the Open System Interconnection (OSI), which is a network protocol.

Repository Style

This style is composed of two main components. The first one is a central data structure that represents the current state of the program, and the second one is represented as a group of independent components that manage the central data structure. This is an effective style to manage large amounts of data and share it. Some examples of this style are information systems, programming environments, or graphical editors.
The event-based style is also known as implicit invocation.
It's designed to work hierarchically among layers. Each layer sends and receives messages from layers above and below.
It's a style composed by a central data structure and a group of components that manage the central data storage.

images.text: Michael: Help me out studying for my styles test! Take this list of questions.
Linda: What's the event-based architecture style about?

Michael: The event-based style is also known as implicit invocation. In this style, components invoke events instead of processes. Events operate the necessary processes implicitly to follow the component's instructions, like daemons. The characteristics of this style involve hooking up a particular process to an event, and also connectors that include procedure calls to bind such processes. Finally, in this style, we can find modules that provide a collection of procedures with a set of events.
Linda: What are its advantages and disadvantages?

Michael: Well, it's easily introduced into a system by including the events, it's a strong support for reuse, and it makes system evolution easier. On the other hand, components don't know how other components react and they relinquish control over computations performed in the system.
Linda: What's the layered systems architecture style about?

Michael: It's designed to work hierarchically among layers. Each layer sends and receives messages from layers above and below; this system is seen as a whole and it's able to provide detailed information about each layer. The characteristics involve clearness in the functionality of each layer and a constant stream of data flow.
Linda: Mention its advantages and disadvantages.

Michael: It's well-organized, layers have a defined task and they aren't dependent. Unfortunately, it's difficult to structure a layered system when it's intended to restrict communication to adjacent layers.
Linda: What's the repository architecture style?

Michael: It's a style composed by a central data structure and a group of components that manage the central data storage. It can be represented with a scheme of a blackboard architecture. It's used to back up information, manage a large amount of data, and share it among users.
